title: The PIMMUR Principles: Ensuring Validity in Collective Behavior of LLM Societies

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating experimental instructions from 42 studies using an LLM-based 'Minimal-Control Test' to detect explicit behavioral steering, and ablating these instructions in multi-agent case studies to show that 'emergent' behaviors vanish without researcher prompting.

Using an 'Unawareness Test' to query LLMs on whether they can infer the underlying hypothesis of an experimental prompt, and demonstrating that models artificially conform to theoretical expectations (e.g., Heider's balance theory) when the experimental intent is transparent.

Simulating a fake news propagation network and manipulating prompts to either explicitly mandate confirmation bias, provide neutral instructions, or reverse the bias, then measuring the resulting population-level belief convergence.

Assigning unique psychometric profiles (Big Five personality traits) to agents in a social network growth simulation to prevent agents from forming connections based merely on latent linguistic preferences for specific arbitrary names.
